input: Start a neighborhood watch group on the street

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this covers just one street, a few blocks, or a wider area changes how many people to recruit, how to structure meetings, and how to divide responsibilities.
Whether the user is starting from scratch with no existing interest vs. already having a few committed neighbors dramatically changes the first steps — cold outreach vs. building on momentum.
The reason for starting the group (recent crime, general prevention, community building) shapes the tone, urgency, and focus of all communications and activities.
Available time to dedicate to this (e.g., a few hours a week vs. minimal) affects how formal the structure can be and how quickly it can launch.
Whether the user wants to affiliate with an official program (e.g., a police-backed scheme) or run an informal group changes the registration steps, resources available, and credibility.
The preferred communication channel (group chat, email list, physical noticeboard, app) determines the tools needed and affects how likely neighbors are to actually participate.
What 'done well' looks like — a certain number of households signed up, a first meeting held, a communication channel active — sets the concrete milestones to plan toward.

gold.taskTitle: Start a neighborhood watch group on your street
gold.taskDescription: Organize and launch a functioning neighborhood watch group for the user's street, covering setup, recruitment, and ongoing coordination.

questions.title: How many households do you want to include?
questions.description: Clarify the geographic scope — just your immediate street, a few surrounding blocks, or a broader neighbourhood — to determine recruitment scale and group structure.

questions.title: Have any neighbours already shown interest in joining?
questions.description: Establish whether the user is starting from zero or already has a small core group, which determines whether the first step is outreach or organisation.

questions.title: What is the main reason you want to start this group?
questions.description: Identify the driving motivation — recent incidents, general safety prevention, or community connection — to shape the tone and focus of all communications.

questions.title: How many hours per week can you dedicate to this?
questions.description: Understand the user's time availability to calibrate how formal, structured, and fast-moving the launch plan should be.

questions.title: Do you want to register with an official police-backed scheme?
questions.description: Determine whether the group should formally affiliate with a local authority or police neighbourhood watch programme, or operate as an informal resident-led group.

questions.title: Which communication channel do you prefer for the group?
questions.description: Pin down the tool for ongoing communication — WhatsApp/Signal group, email list, a neighbourhood app like Nextdoor, or a physical noticeboard — to choose the right setup steps.

questions.title: What would a successful launch look like to you?
questions.description: Define the concrete milestone the user has in mind — a minimum number of households signed up, a first meeting held, or a communication channel up and running.
